description.summary: surfaces only the person can answer

protocol.description:
The desktop shell shows a confirmation or a notice on a trusted surface. The compositor draws it above every other surface, keeps agent seats and synthetic input away from it, accepts an answer only from physical input and only after the surface has been on screen, unobscured, for its arming time. The decision itself travels from the shell to its caller over D-Bus; this protocol only tells the shell when an answer is trustworthy.
Not served yet: casement does not advertise this global today, so the shell cannot rely on it to tell a person's answer from a program's. Nothing may rely on a promise made here until the server lands.
A trusted surface anchors to a window by its ext_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1 identifier string, because the shell creates trusted surfaces on a different connection from the one that holds its toplevel handles, and no Wayland object crosses connections.
This protocol is a draft. Until it is declared stable, version 1 may change in place with every client and the server updated together.

entry.name: role_taken
entry.summary: the wl_surface already has a role

entry.name: unknown_toplevel
entry.summary: no toplevel has the given identifier

description.summary: what the surface asks of the person

entry.name: window
entry.summary: attached to the named toplevel, as a sheet

entry.name: centre
entry.summary: centred on the output with the pointer

request.name: get_trusted

description.summary: give a surface the trusted role

request.description: `toplevel` is the ext_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1 identifier of the window for the `window` anchor, and empty for `centre`. `arm_ms` is how long the surface must be presented and unobscured before an answer counts.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Trusted surfaces already created stay valid.

interface.name: quire_trusted_surface_v1
interface.description: Events arrive in order: `presented`, then `armed`, then `answered_by_physical` or `withdrawn`. `withdrawn` is the last event.

description.summary: why the compositor took the surface down

event.name: presented
event.description: Sent when the surface is first shown unobscured.

event.name: armed
event.description: Sent when the surface has been presented and unobscured for its arming time.

event.name: answered_by_physical

description.summary: the person answered with physical input

event.description: `serial` is the serial of the input event the compositor delivered to the surface; the shell sends the answer it carries only when this event names it.

arg.name: serial
arg.summary: serial of the physical input event

event.name: withdrawn
event.description: The last event; the client destroys the object.

request.name: destroy
request.description: The wl_surface loses the trusted role.
